news.text: 1 July saw the foreign and defence ministers of the Soviet Union, Poland, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, Romania, and Bulgaria meet in Prague to sign the protocol officially dissolving the **Warsaw Pact**. Established in 1955 as the communist military counterweight to NATO, the formal dissolution ended **36 years of Cold War confrontation** across Europe.
news.youtube: Warsaw Pact officially dissolved Prague July 1991 news

news.text: 7 July saw 22-year-old German tennis sensation **Michael Stich** shock world number one and compatriot Boris Becker in straight sets (6–4, 7–6, 6–4) on Centre Court to win his maiden **Wimbledon men's singles title**. Stich became only the second German man ever to lift the trophy, having already defeated world number two Stefan Edberg in the **semi-finals**.
news.youtube: Michael Stich vs Boris Becker Wimbledon 1991 final highlights

news.text: 13 July saw Canadian rocker Bryan Adams ascend to number one on the UK Singles Chart with the epic power ballad ***(Everything I Do) I Do It for You***. Featured on the soundtrack to Kevin Costner's blockbuster film ***Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves***, the soaring track embarked on an unprecedented, record-breaking **16 consecutive weeks** atop the **British charts**.
news.wiki: (Everything I Do) I Do It for You
news.youtube: Bryan Adams Everything I Do I Do It For You official video 1991

news.text: 14 July saw World Championship Wrestling present ***The Great American Bash 1991*** at the Baltimore Arena. Following the shock firing of champion **Ric Flair** by WCW executive Jim Herd (with Flair taking the physical Big Gold Belt to the WWF), **Lex Luger** defeated Barry Windham inside a steel cage to capture the vacant WCW World Heavyweight Championship, turning heel by **aligning with Harley Race**.
news.youtube: Lex Luger vs Barry Windham Great American Bash 1991 steel cage match

news.text: 31 July saw US President George H.W. Bush and Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev sign the landmark **START I treaty** (Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty) at the Kremlin in Moscow. Mandating the first bilateral reduction of strategic nuclear arsenals in history, the treaty required both superpowers to dismantle approximately **80% of all strategic nuclear warheads** in existence.

gaming.title: Final Fantasy IV
gaming.reviewQuote: A dramatic leap forward for narrative gaming. The Active Time Battle system and Nobuo Uematsu's orchestral score elevate RPGs to high art.
gaming.headline: Dark Knights, Active Time Battle, and Square's 16-Bit Storytelling Leap
gaming.gameplay: Released on 19 July 1991 for the Super Famicom in Japan (and later localised as *Final Fantasy II* in North America), *Final Fantasy IV* revolutionised JRPGs. Conceived by **Hironobu Sakaguchi** with battle system design by Hiroyuki Ito, the game introduced the iconic **Active Time Battle (ATB)** system, replacing rigid turn-based turns with real-time gauges. Players guided dark knight Cecil Harvey on a moral journey of redemption, transitioning to a paladin alongside memorable allies like Kain Highwind and Rydia to thwart the mysterious sorcerer Golbez.
gaming.reception: Critically celebrated upon release, the title earned high acclaim from *Famitsu* and import magazines. Reviewers praised its operatic dramatic pacing, heartbreaking character sacrifices, Mode 7 airship scaling, and Nobuo Uematsu's peerless 44-track musical score, featuring the timeless 'Theme of Love'.
gaming.impact: Setting the narrative and mechanical blueprint for 1990s JRPGs, *Final Fantasy IV* established Square as the supreme master of interactive storytelling and spearheaded the golden age of 16-bit role-playing games.
